ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In square $ABCD$, diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at point $O$. Point $E$ is on $DO$ with $DE = 2EO$. Connect $AE$ and fold $\triangle ADE$ along $AD$ to get $\triangle ADE'$. Point $F$ is the midpoint of $AE$, and connect $E'F$. If $DE = 2\sqrt{2}$, what is the area of $\triangle AFE'$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect $EE'$,\\
since quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a square,\\
it follows that $OA=OD$, $\angle ADO=45^\circ$, $\angle AOD=90^\circ$\\
Given $DE=2\sqrt{2}$, $DE=2EO$\\
it follows that $OD=OA=3\sqrt{2}$\\
thus, ${S}_{\triangle ADE}=\frac{1}{2}DE\times OA=6$\\
According to the problem, $\angle ADE'=\angle ADO=45^\circ$, $DE=DE'=2\sqrt{2}$\\
thus, ${S}_{\triangle DEE'}=\frac{1}{2}DE\times DE=4$, ${S}_{\text{quadrilateral} AED{E}'}=2{S}_{\triangle ADE}=12$\\
therefore, ${S}_{\triangle AEE'}={S}_{\text{quadrilateral}AED{E}'}-{S}_{\triangle DEE'}=8$\\
Also, since $F$ is the midpoint of $AE$\\
it follows that ${S}_{\triangle AEE'F}=\frac{1}{2}{S}_{\triangle AEE'}=\boxed{4}$
